title: Packed GF(p)[x] FLINT divrem
objective: Route public packed prime-field polynomial quotient and remainder through one declared FLINT nmod_poly_divrem computation while preserving the typed-Python dynamic fallback and Sage-compatible errors

handoff.summary: Public packed GF(p)[x] quotient and remainder now use one declared, transactional FLINT nmod_poly_divrem call whenever the compiled kernel is available, while the existing typed-Python long division remains the tested dynamic fallback. The generated boundary is host-isolated with one public crossing and zero callbacks. On this host, warm median public quo_rem is about 0.6-0.9 ms for degree 1800 by 300 and 1.6-1.9 ms for degree 5000 by 1000, down from roughly 6 ms and 22 ms respectively.
risks: The portable dynamic fallback remains intentionally much slower for large inputs; correctness is differential-tested, and a future Wasm FLINT package can use the same declaration.
The broad FFI test has unrelated baseline expectations for the newly integrated M4RI declaration; the divrem-focused test, deterministic FFI check, architecture check, and strict baselib checks pass.
next_steps: Integrate this branch and rerun the broad portable and native suites in the fully synchronized integration tree.
Consider routing prime-field polynomial power through FLINT after a separate measured crossover audit.
